# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- A probe is a task of a brief that builds a change to answer a question and does not land it. Commit its change as a patch file, with its report and programs, in the `probes/` folder that the brief names, and no edit of the original tree. If the brief names no folder, commit nothing of the probe: give the patch's path and the report in your final message.
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- Do not commit `.claude/worktrees/` or `.claude/agents/`, which show as untracked in a fresh clone.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, also gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree leaves its branch. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The platform rebuilds a lost container from `blinded-fable`.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

# The report and the record

## What every report holds

Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.

A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.

A fact is a finding that is an established property of the tree, the language, the library or their tools, and that later work builds on. A defect also gets its ledger row, and a fact about it may cite the row.

A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.

Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:

- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
- **For FACTS.** Each fact that your work established, in the hand-over form of "Writing to the record". If your brief let you write FACTS, give instead the number of each entry that you added or rewrote. If your work established no fact, write "none".
- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.

## At a point to report

- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
- Then finish the work.
- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.

## Timings and citations

- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.

## POSITIONS and FACTS

POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.

Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".

## The gap ledger

The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.

- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.

Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.

A row states its gap as it stands now. A note adds a fact. If your work changes what a row says, write the row's whole new line with `rewrite` (below), not a note that tells the repair.

The heading reader of `ledger.py` does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:

    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh

- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.

A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.

Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:

    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE

## Writing to the record

- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`, never by hand. `add` gives a new entry its number, and `set` rewrites an entry. The tool writes the entry to `FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md`, and its earlier text to the history file beside it. It commits nothing: commit both files in one commit. Its header gives its usage.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, add each fact as a new entry in the section of its topic, in the commit that establishes it. Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers. Point the entry to that section, by your report's file and the section's heading. If your report is only your final message, hand the fact over instead. Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work.
- If your brief does not let you write FACTS, hand each fact over in the "For FACTS" item of your report, with:
  - the fact as it stands now, in one sentence;
  - what it means for the work;
  - the number that a decision rests on, if any, with what it counts; if its parts belong to different ledger rows, the part of each row;
  - the test that fails if the fact stops holding, or the command and the output that show it;
  - the section of your report that holds the detail.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, rewrite a wrong entry in place. Otherwise say in your hand-over that the entry is wrong, with the evidence.
- POSITIONS holds each of the curator's decisions, in one place. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.

Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.

    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

To add a row:

1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

To change a row:

- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N. It refuses a note that takes the row past 1,200 characters, or its notes cell past 700 characters. `$L note N TEXT --check` writes nothing. It says whether TEXT fits, and how many characters the notes and the row have left now and would have left with TEXT. These counts include the separator that the tool adds. It exits 0 if TEXT fits, and 1 if not. Run it before a long note, or before a note on a row near its limits. If TEXT does not fit, shorten it, or cut the notes with `rewrite` (below).
- `$L rewrite N FILE` replaces row N with the whole line in FILE, a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with N or `?` in its number cell. Use it to correct the claim, cut the notes or change the reproducer. The tool checks the line against the template and keeps the old line in the history file.
- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it. NAME can also be a file under `explorations/coordinator/tools/`, or `none` with `--note REASON`. For a `CONTESTED` row, add `--settled TEXT`, which names what settled its question.
- `$L landing-check BASE` prints each problem, and exits 1 on any. Run it when your brief asks for it. It checks the whole ledger against the template, so a broken row that BASE already had counts too. The problems are a row that breaks the template, an `XXX` test deleted or renamed while a row that is not closed names it, a row that is not closed though a commit says it fixed it, and a FACTS or POSITIONS entry that disagrees with a row's status.

## The repository's history

- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.
- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's. After the tag `sealed-tree`, commit `75cca6683`, the revival began to fix the team's code, test first. Before it, the revival changed mainly the build and the toolchain.
- `git diff a874948ac -- FILE` shows what the revival changed in a file, and `git diff 75cca6683 -- FILE` what it changed after the tag.
- If the commands above fail, run `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`. It prints `true` in a shallow clone, where these commits do not resolve. There, a copyright header of Sun Microsystems or Oracle, as in `Library/Format.fss`, marks a file that the team made, but not which of its lines the port or the revival changed. If your task needs those lines, say in your report that the clone is shallow.
- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a `git log` of a directory stops at a cut and misses the team's earlier commits. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.
- Commit `8fe1daa8f` copied a third-party port of the tree to Java 9 onto the team's last commit, `a874948ac`. Give its lines no credit, and name no author of it in any text that you commit. In a reconstruction of authorship, attribute nothing of it to anyone.

# The gate

The gate runs the seven steps below on one tree, in about 25 minutes. It is green if every step passes, and red if one fails. If a step fails, run the rest, so that the summary holds every step's result.

## What it writes

The summary, `summary.txt`, has one tab-separated row for each suite: `track/suite`, tests, failures, errors, skipped. Below the rows, lines that start with `#` give each log's `BUILD` and `Total time:` lines, the machine that ran the gate (`# machine`), the atomic runs and the ladder's comparison. A landed summary can also end with `# microgpt-walk` lines: the `VERDICT:` and `rc=` lines of the microGPT walk check (`interpreter.md`, "The model program"), run on the landed tree. Add them only if your brief asks for the microGPT walk check on the landed tree.

If your brief asks you to land a gate's results, put them in a new `gate/` folder in `explorations/compile-ladder/`, under the `climb-batch-` name that your brief gives, in the form of the newest one: `summary.txt`, and in `ladder/` the files `ladder.tsv`, `microgpt-phase.md`, `comparison.txt` and `microgpt-comparison.txt`. The next gate compares with the newest summary there or in `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/`, and finds no other. Land them in a commit that changes nothing else that the gate reads.

Steps 5 and 7 use shell functions that `explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh` defines. The file runs nothing. In each Bash call of steps 5 and 7, set up the call as `build-and-caches.md` says, which sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the tree's root. Then source the file, from the root:

    source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh

## When to run it

Your brief says whether you run the gate. If it does not ask, run only your own tests (`tests-running.md`).

If it asks, first check whether the newest gate still holds for your tree. A gate's tables stay valid until the tree changes under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or in `build.xml`, outside the test files. A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` file directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory. The commit that landed the newest summary changed nothing that the gate reads. Commit your tree, then run this command. It prints each path, test files excepted, changed since that commit:

    G=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt')
    git diff --name-only $G HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml \
        | grep -v -E '^ProjectFortress/([^/]*_)?tests/[^/]*\.(fss|fsi|test)$'

- If it prints a path, run the gate.
- If not, the newest gate holds. Run only the changed test files, through `harness-one.sh` and `junit.sh` (`tests-running.md`).

## The steps

Run these steps from the tree's root. Keep the logs of steps 2 and 4 in `tmp/gate/`, as `compileAll.txt`, `testFast.txt`, `testSystem.txt` and `testSpecData.txt`.

1. Read the Avail column of `df -h /`. Warning: deleting `/tmp/fortress*rats` can break other live runs. If the column shows less than 1 GB, delete `/tmp/fortress*rats`, `ProjectFortress/test-tmp` and `ProjectFortress/test-caches`, and read it again. If it still shows less than 500 MB, stop and report.
2. Run `rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS tmp/gate && mkdir -p tmp/gate`, then `ant compileAll`.
3. If the build printed `Caches <tree>/default_repository/caches started again, empty`, run the library order (`build-and-caches.md`). If not, and a source of the compiler's library changed since the caches were filled, take its step in `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library". Then copy the caches twice for the ladder regression, before anything else compiles into them:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

4. Run `ant testFast`, then `ant testSystem`, then `ant testSpecData`. All three must have zero failures. In `ant testSystem`, `tests/XXXAtomicNestedReadsKeptWalk` can print `PASS` and fail with 'Missing expected failure': its expected failure depends on a race (ledger row 1004). The gate is then red, as for any failure. Cite the row in your report.
5. Write the summary: `gate_summary tmp/gate tmp/gate/summary.txt`. Compare it: `gate_compare "$(last_landed_summary)" tmp/gate/summary.txt`. It prints a line for a suite with failures or errors, a suite with no tests, a suite whose count of tests fell, and a suite that is gone. Each such line makes the gate red. A count that rose prints nothing.
6. Do the atomic runs, and append their lines to the summary.
7. Do the ladder regression.

## The atomic runs

The atomic runs compile twenty-two programs, and run each one three times at four threads. They need the library's jars in the tree's caches (`build-and-caches.md`). Run them from `ProjectFortress/`:

    for p in AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG \
             AlsoArmThrowsJoinsCompiled CallArgumentsForkCompiled AtomicOwnWriteNestedCompiled \
             AtomicNestedSameBodyCompiled NestedAtomicAbortCompiled AtomicNestedViewCompiled \
             AtomicSharedReadsCompiled AtomicThrowRevertsCompiled \
             atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 \
             nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2 ; do
      d=other_compiler_tests ; [ -f compiler_tests/$p.fss ] && d=compiler_tests
      timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile $d/$p.fss >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" ; continue ; }
      for i in 1 2 3 ; do
        out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$?
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && { out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$? ; }
        case "$out" in *FAIL*) r=FAIL ;; *PASS*) r=PASS ;; *) r="NO-PASS rc=$rc" ;; esac
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && r=TIMEOUT-TWICE
        echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 $r"
      done
    done

The gate is red on any FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE.

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

## Comparing with an earlier run

- `ant testSystem` runs in four shards, the summary's rows `system-0` to `system-3`. A shard takes the files by their place in a sorted list, so an added file moves every later file to another shard. When you compare by hand, compare only the sum of the four. `gate_compare` sums them.
- In printed output, mask only these differences: the `Operation took <n>ms` line, a Java line number in a stack frame, an object's identity hash (`@` and hex digits), and a position in a library file that your change moved. In your report, list each test with a masked difference, and the kinds masked in it.
- If your brief asks you to compare the interpreter tests with a base run, use the two scripts in `explorations/coordinator/tools/count-run/`. `count-run.sh` runs every `ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss` under walk, one JVM per test: run it once on the base commit and once after your edit. `compare-normalised.py` compares the two runs, with the last three masks above. Each script's header gives its usage.

(* A loop body and a function expression inside an object's method read and write the object's var field itself, not a copy made when the body or the function was built. *)
component VarFieldCapturedCompiled
export Executable

object Ctr(var n: ZZ32)
    var m: ZZ32 = 10
    getter count(): ZZ32 = n
    getter other(): ZZ32 = m
    fill(k: ZZ32): () = for i <- 1#k do atomic do n := n + 1 end end
    reader(): () -> ZZ32 = fn () => n + m
    writer(): ZZ32 -> () = fn (x: ZZ32) => do n := x; m := x + 1 end
    set(x: ZZ32): () = do n := x; m := x end
end

run(): () = do
    c = Ctr(1)
    r = c.reader()
    w = c.writer()
    first = r()
    c.set(5)
    second = r()
    w(7)
    third = c.count + c.other
    c.fill(1000)
    fourth = c.count
    if (first = 11) AND (second = 10) AND (third = 15) AND (fourth = 1007) then
        println("PASS")
    else
        println("FAIL: a function's reads " first " and " second " (expected 11 and 10), after a function's write "
                third " (expected 15), after a loop's writes " fourth " (expected 1007)")
    end
  end

end
EOF

"""Generate the probe's shadow sources from the tracked ones by textual patch.

Nothing tracked is modified: the copies are written under <shadow-src>, compiled
into <shadow-classes>, and put FIRST on the run-time classpath, ahead of
ProjectFortress/build.  usage: shadow-patch.py <src-root> <shadow-src>

Three shadows, each one edit:

  DesugarPhase         tolerate a missing type-checker map, so DESUGAR can run
                       with TYPECHECK left out of the phase order (Desugarer
                       passes the map on only to CaseExprDesugarer).
  CodeGenerationPhase  wrap the whole per-component body in try/catch, and print
                       the stack trace of whatever ends it.
  CodeGen              wrap the per-declaration loop of forComponent in
                       try/catch, so one refused declaration does not end the
                       run and the whole hole list comes out of one pass.
"""
import sys, io, os

src, shadow = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

def patch(rel, edits, out):
    t = io.open(os.path.join(src, rel), encoding="utf-8").read()
    for old, new in edits:
        assert old in t, rel + ": anchor not found: " + old[:60]
        t = t.replace(old, new, 1)
    p = os.path.join(shadow, out)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(t)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- DesugarPhase

"        Desugarer.ComponentResult componentDSR = Desugarer.desugarComponents(previous.components(), apiEnv, previous.typeCheckers());",

content.content:
== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT=/home/user/fortress-atomic-expr-field/tmp/rung-atomic-expr-field/ladder/root
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT=/home/user/fortress-atomic-expr-field/tmp/rung-atomic-expr-field/ladder
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the raw compile/run outputs of run-ladder.sh into the ladder table.

Reads  explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv  and  raw/<corpus>/<file>.{compile,run}
Writes explorations/compile-ladder/ladder.tsv    (one row per file, diffable)
       explorations/compile-ladder/summary.txt   (the counts and the rankings)

Phase vocabulary, and where each decision comes from:
  parse        a parse-stage refusal (Rats! "Syntax Error", the precedence
               resolver's "Resolution of operator ... failed")
  disambiguate an unresolved or ambiguous name (TypeDisambiguator.java:363,380
               "X is undefined."; "Type name may refer to";
               GraphRepository.java:417 "Could not find an implementation for API")
  typecheck    the Scala checker (TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:95,119
               "Unbound type:"; "Could not check call to"; "Ill-formed type")
  codegen      CodeGen.sayWhat (CodeGen.java:1550-1562 "Can't compile") or any
               CompilerError raised from the codegen packages
  link         `fortress run` fails to load or link the compiled component
  run          `fortress run` throws or exits non-zero
  pass         exit 0, no `fail`/`FAIL` in the output, no exception
               (the interpreter suite's own criterion, FileTests.java:367-371)
"""

import os, re, sys, collections

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(ROOT, "raw")

# Source this in every shell that runs Fortress:  source explorations/experiment/env.sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=1
# bin/fortress defaults to -Xmx256m (gap ledger row 67); the checks at 4 threads override FORTRESS_THREADS on the command line
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m"
# every grammar-importing run leaves a 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory behind (RatsUtil.getTempDir); 723 of them filled the disk allowance on 2026-09-15.
# Remove only those that no run can still be using: nothing in it written for an hour, and no java process now
# running started before its last write (a run makes its directory after it starts, and reads it until it ends).
(
  oldest=$(ps -C java -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  now=$(date +%s)
  find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'fortress*rats' -mmin +60 -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
  while read -r t d ; do
    [ -n "$oldest" ] && [ "${t%.*}" -ge $(( now - oldest )) ] && continue
    [ -n "$(find "$d" -newermt '60 minutes ago' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && continue
    rm -rf "$d"
  done
)

Evidence: fork A1, "as a top-level `var` is"; PFieldInTask and PFieldClosure, old against new. The cost in naming: `isAMutableStaticBinding()` is now true for a var field. 3. **The cell is made in the constructor by a `FieldVar` whose write wraps the value** (`firstWrite`), since the constructor's code assigns each field through the `VarCodeGen` it is given (`forExprsSerial`, `genParallelExprs`). Way not taken: a flag in `MutableFieldVar.assignValue` that tells the first write, which a method's write could not be told from. 4. **An immutable field of the body becomes a `FieldVar`;** its JVM field keeps `ACC_PUBLIC` without `ACC_FINAL`, so that no flag of an existing class file changes. Way not taken: `ACC_FINAL` on it, which is right and is a change to an immutable field, a reserved point. 5. **`VarFieldCapturedCompiled` is a test of its own,** not more assertions in `AtomicFieldCompiled`. Reason: it fails at one thread on the old code, so its failing run is certain, and `AtomicFieldCompiled`'s is a race. 6. **The field test's own atomic write of `torn` is a block,** not an atomic expression, so that on the base the test fails by the field's race and not at the code generator's wall. 7. **`ant testQuick` for "the whole compiled suite":** the compiler, othercompiler and library tracks, all of which compile objects. Way not taken: `ant testCompiler`, without the library track. ## Defects, each with its home 1. Row 875, the atomic expression refused: home 1, repaired; `compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled`. 2. Row 319, a var field outside the transaction: home 1, repaired; `compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled`. 3. Not in the ledger: a loop body or a function expression inside an object's method reads and writes a copy of the object's var field (PFieldInTask: `0` of 40,000 on the old code at one thread). Home 1, repaired; `compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled`. No row: the change that measured it repairs it. 4. Row 112, a value object with a var field: the compiled path compiles it too, and `V(1) === V(1)` went from `true` to `false`, since `SEQV` compares a value object field by field and a cell is equal only to itself (`nativeHelpers/equalityRule.java:83`). The specification forbids the program (`objects.tex:35`), and the row holds the gap; a note for it is in record.md. No test: the row's reproducer is `none`, and what the checker should say is not written anywhere. 5. Row 397, a tuple-typed var field's setter: unchanged, its `XXX` test still an expected failure. 6. Row 641, the check before every access: now also on a var field; the row's whole new line is in record.md. Not timed. ## For FACTS In record.md. ## Commands worked out - The object's class of a compiled test, for `javap`: `unzip default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/.jar` into a scratch folder (the jar's names use `$`, and a generic template's name holds `⟦⟧`; copy that file to a plain name before `javap -p -c`). - A compiled `.test` through the harness on the old code: from `ProjectFortress/`, `old-fortress.sh junit compiler_tests/X.test`, the skill's form. The code and the tests are in commit `67b1030c48` on `wip/rung-atomic-expr-field`; every run below that is called "new" ran on that code. The machine: 4 cores, Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1. ## What changed and why 1. **The atomic expression** (`CodeGen.java:1870-1877`). The parser writes `atomic do ... end` as a `Block` marked atomic (`parser/DelimitedExpr.rats:155-163`) and `atomic e`, for any other body, as an `AtomicExpr` (`parser/Expression.rats:737-738`). The code generator compiled the first and had no case for the second, so `defaultCase` refused it. The new member `forAtomicExpr` makes the atomic block that holds the body alone, the node the parser makes for `atomic do e end`, and hands it to `forAtomicBlock`. The block's value is its last expression's (`doStatements`, `CodeGen.java:1627`), so the expression's value is its body's. 2. **A var field** (`CodeGen.java:4827-4850`, `:4865-4903`; `VarCodeGen.java:202-239`, `:325`). An object's `var` value parameter and `var` field of its body are kept in a `MutableFValue` cell. The object's JVM field holds the cell, is `public final`, and is written once, by the constructor (`MutableFieldVar.firstWrite`, `VarCodeGen.java:223`). `MutableFieldVar` is now a `MutableStaticBinding` whose cell is reached through the object, so a read and a write emit the code of a top-level `var`: the check `BaseTask.inATransaction()`, then `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` on the cell inside a transaction, or the cell's `getValue`/`setValue` outside one. A field that is not `var` is a `FieldVar`, as an immutable value parameter was, with the bytecode it had. 3. **A field captured by a loop body or a function expression.** Every nested code-generation context (a task, a closure) asks `isAMutableStaticBinding()` to decide whether it captures a cell or a copy (`CodeGen.java:5171`, `:5286`, `:5351` at the base). Because `MutableFieldVar` now is one, a loop body or a function expression inside an object's method captures the field's cell. On the base it captured a copy of the value, so a write from a loop body inside the object's own method was lost at one thread too. This defect was not in the ledger; the cell repairs it, and `compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled` asserts it. ## The failing runs and the passing run The tests were written first and run through the harness on the base's code, in runs that ended before the edit was first built (00:44:54 to 00:45:05 UTC; the build of the edit started after). FORTRESS_THREADS=4; tree c1ce2a35e1 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled.fss:8:9-69: Can't compile AtomicExpr at ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled.fss:8.9 F. run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled (1204ms) FAIL: value parameter 34631 (expected 40000 ), body field 80007 (expected 80007 ), torn reads 0 , generic value parameter 40000 (expected 40000 ), immutable fields Tests run: 4, Failures: 3, Errors: 0 `VarFieldCapturedCompiled` was written after the edit was built, so its failing run is on the old code through the harness. ## For FACTS

**A compiled object's `var` field lives in a cell that the object holds, and an atomic expression is its body in an atomic block.** On the compiled path a `var` value parameter or `var` field of an object is a `MutableFValue` cell in a `public final` JVM field, made by the constructor; each read and write checks `BaseTask.inATransaction()` and goes through the transaction or the cell, by the code of a top-level `var` (`VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar`, a `MutableStaticBinding`), and a loop body or a function expression in the object's method captures the cell. A field without `var` holds its value and has no check. `atomic e` is compiled by `forAtomicBlock` on the block that holds `e`. What it means: a change of the transaction's variable code reaches fields with no second edit, and a new kind of nested context must capture a var field's cell as it does a top-level `var`'s. ## Revival change

### The change

- **An atomic expression compiles.** The team's code generator compiled `atomic do ... end` and had no case for `atomic e` over any other body: its `defaultCase` refused the node, 'Can't compile AtomicExpr' (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1776` and `forAtomicBlock` at `:1835`, at `c1ce2a35e1`). The tree now compiles `atomic e` as the atomic block that holds `e`, with the value of `e` (`compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled`). The reason: the specification gives the atomic expression its body's value and makes all its reads and writes one step (`Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex`, section "Atomic Expressions"), walk runs it, and the one library writes it (`Library/OneShotFlag.fss:18`).
- **A compiled object's `var` field is tracked by a transaction, at the cost of a check on every access.** The team's code generator read an object's field with a bare `GETFIELD` and wrote it with a bare `PUTFIELD`, a `var` field as any other (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:174-236` at `c1ce2a35e1`), so an `atomic` block did not track it: 40,000 `atomic do n := n + 1 end` on a field from a parallel loop gave 34,631 to 39,313 at four threads. The tree now keeps a `var` value parameter or `var` field in a cell that the object holds, read and written as a top-level `var` is; each access, outside `atomic` too, first asks whether a transaction is running (`compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled`). A field without `var` is as it was. The reason: mutable fields of reference objects are mutable locations (`Specification/basic/evaluation/memory-ops.tex`, section "Memory and Memory Operations"), an atomic expression's reads and writes are all one step, and walk is exact on the same program.
- **A loop body or a function expression in an object's method works on the object's `var` field, not on a copy.** The team's code generator gave each task and closure a copy of a field's value, made when the task or closure was built, so a write from a loop body in the object's own method was lost, at one thread too, and a function expression read a stale value: `for i <- 1#k do atomic do n := n + 1 end end` in a method left `n` at 0. The tree now gives the task or closure the field's cell (`compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled`). The reason: the measured failure, and walk's result on the same program.
- **Do not give a `value` object a `var` field in a compiled program.** The specification forbids it (`Specification/basic/objects.tex`, section "Value Objects") and nothing refuses it; with the field in a cell, two such objects built alike are no longer strictly equivalent, `V(1) === V(1)` is `false`.

# Rung A, rung-atomic-expr-field: atomic as an expression, and a var field inside a transaction - problem: the code generator refuses `Library/OneShotFlag.fss`'s `tryOnce`, 'Can't compile AtomicExpr' (ledger row 875), and `atomic do n := n + 1 end` on a field loses updates at four threads, 29,456 and 39,276 of 40,000 (ledger row 319; the batch record's section for this rung) — Library/OneShotFlag.fss:18 - spec: an atomic expression's value is its body's, and its reads and writes are one step with respect to every thread outside — Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:36-43; mutable locations are mutable variables and mutable fields of reference objects — Specification/basic/evaluation/memory-ops.tex:48-49 - precedent: a top-level `var`, kept in a `MutableFValue` cell that its class's field holds, read and written through the transaction — ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:313 - deviation: none from the specification's spelling; from the precedent, the cell is reached through the object (`ALOAD 0`, `GETFIELD`) and is made in the object's constructor, not in a class initializer — ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:216-235 - historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java — none One launch worked this rung. The code and the tests are in commit `67b1030c48` on `wip/rung-atomic-expr-field`; every run below that is called "new" ran on that code. The machine: 4 cores, Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1. ## What changed and why 1. **The atomic expression** (`CodeGen.java:1870-1877`). The parser writes `atomic do ... end` as a `Block` marked atomic (`parser/DelimitedExpr.rats:155-163`) and `atomic e`, for any other body, as an `AtomicExpr` (`parser/Expression.rats:737-738`). The code generator compiled the first and had no case for the second, so `defaultCase` refused it. The new member `forAtomicExpr` makes the atomic block that holds the body alone, the node the parser makes for `atomic do e end`, and hands it to `forAtomicBlock`. The block's value is its last expression's (`doStatements`, `CodeGen.java:1627`), so the expression's value is its body's. 2. **A var field** (`CodeGen.java:4827-4850`, `:4865-4903`; `VarCodeGen.java:202-239`, `:325`). An object's `var` value parameter and `var` field of its body are kept in a `MutableFValue` cell. The object's JVM field holds the cell, is `public final`, and is written once, by the constructor (`MutableFieldVar.firstWrite`, `VarCodeGen.java:223`). `MutableFieldVar` is now a `MutableStaticBinding` whose cell is reached through the object, so a read and a write emit the code of a top-level `var`: the check `BaseTask.inATransaction()`, then `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` on the cell inside a transaction, or the cell's `getValue`/`setValue` outside one. A field that is not `var` is a `FieldVar`, as an immutable value parameter was, with the bytecode it had. 3. **A field captured by a loop body or a function expression.** Every nested code-generation context (a task, a closure) asks `isAMutableStaticBinding()` to decide whether it captures a cell or a copy (`CodeGen.java:5171`, `:5286`, `:5351` at the base). Because `MutableFieldVar` now is one, a loop body or a function expression inside an object's method captures the field's cell. On the base it captured a copy of the value, so a write from a loop body inside the object's own method was lost at one thread too. This defect was not in the ledger; the cell repairs it, and `compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled` asserts it. ## The failing runs and the passing run The tests were written first and run through the harness on the base's code, in runs that ended before the edit was first built (00:44:54 to 00:45:05 UTC; the build of the edit started after). Command, in the tree at the base's code: `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests AtomicExprCompiled.test AtomicFieldCompiled.test` # junit.sh base 2026-11-17T00:44:54Z; nproc 4; ... Command, from `ProjectFortress/`: `FORTRESS_THREADS=4 explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base35 junit compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled.test` . run .../compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled (611ms) FAIL: a function's reads 11 and 11 (expected 11 and 10), after a function's write 10 (expected 15), after a loop's writes 5 (expected 1007) Tests run: 2, Failures: 1, Errors: 0 The passing run, the last run of the tests after the last change of code. So each of the three kinds of var field loses updates on the old code, and a field read twice in one block once gave two values. ## The whole compiled suite `ant testQuick`, once, on `67b1030c48`, after the last edit of code: [junit] Tests run: 86, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 102.384 sec (library) [junit] Tests run: 263, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 151.884 sec (othercompiler) [junit] Tests run: 1625, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 417.822 sec (compiler) BUILD SUCCESSFUL Total time: 7 minutes 2 seconds `compiler_tests/XXXTupleVarFieldCompiledRungC` (ledger row 397) is among them and still fails as expected: a tuple-typed var field's setter fails verification as before, on old and new alike (program PBoxKinds below). ## The atomic programs on the final tree The loop of the skill's gate.md, "The atomic runs", with the batch's two new programs and `VarFieldCapturedCompiled` added: 25 programs, three runs each at four threads, on `67b1030c48`. 75 lines, each `PASS`; no FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE. For the three new programs: # atomic AtomicExprCompiled run1 threads=4 PASS # atomic AtomicFieldCompiled run1 threads=4 PASS # atomic VarFieldCapturedCompiled run1 threads=4 PASS (and run2 and run3 of each the same). ## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search - The atomic expression belongs in the code generator: the checker types it (`fortress typecheck compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled.fss` exits 0 on the base), walk runs it, and only `CodeGen.defaultCase` refused it. Its place is directly below `forAtomicBlock`, as the batch record assigns. - The field belongs where an object's fields get their code: `forObjectDeclPrePass` builds one `VarCodeGen` for each value parameter and each field of the body, and every read and write of a field in a method goes through it (`forVarRef`, `forAssignment`). A field read from outside the object goes through the getter and setter methods that the desugarer makes, which are methods of the object. No other code in `compiler/codegen/` emits `GETFIELD` or `PUTFIELD` on an object's field (`grep -n 'GETFIELD\|PUTFIELD' CodeGen.java`: task results, closure siblings and RTTI only). - The precedent is the top-level `var` (`VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding`, `generateVarDeclInnerClass` in `CodeGen.java`): a cell held in a final field, the check before each access, the cast after a read. `VarCodeGen.java` holds three classes that emit that check (`LocalMutableVar`, `MutableTaskVarCodeGen`, `MutableStaticBinding`; six methods). # Rung A, rung-atomic-expr-field: the record lines

Code and tests: commit `67b1030c48` on `wip/rung-atomic-expr-field`; the gather's commit on `main` takes its place in the closes below. Detail and every quoted run: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-atomic-expr-field/REPORT.md`.

## Findings

1. **The code generator compiles an atomic expression.** `atomic e`, for a body `e` that is no `do` block, is compiled as the atomic block that holds `e` alone, the node the parser makes for `atomic do e end`; the new member emits no instruction of its own (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1870-1877`). Holds for every body the checker accepts; the expression has the block's limits, among them a `VerifyError` as a call's argument after the first (row 322). Evidence: `compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled` (on the base: 'Can't compile AtomicExpr at ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled.fss:8.9'; on the change: PASS at one thread and at four). For the work: `Library/OneShotFlag.fss:18` is no longer a wall of the code generator; `tryatomic` still is (row 353).
2. **An object's `var` field, a `var` value parameter among them, is inside the transaction of an `atomic` block on the compiled path.** The object's JVM field is `public final` and holds a `MutableFValue` cell; a read and a write emit a top-level `var`'s code on that cell (`VarCodeGen.java:202-239`, `:313-410`; `CodeGen.java:4827-4850`, `:4865-4903`). Holds for a value parameter, a field of the body, and a generic object's value parameter whose type is the type parameter (run at `String`, a tuple type and an arrow type). An immutable field holds its value and reads by the same two instructions as before. Evidence: `compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled` (old code at four threads: 'value parameter 39220 (expected 40000), body field 67439 (expected 80007), torn reads 1, generic value parameter 39313 (expected 40000)'; the change: PASS at one thread and at four, and in three runs of the atomic loop). For the work: the one library's `OneShot`, `Box[\T\](var val: T)` and `String.fss`'s var fields are tracked once the compiled path reads them.
3. **A loop body or a function expression inside an object's method reads and writes the object's `var` field itself.** On the base each captured a copy of the value when it was built, so `fill(k) = for i <- 1#k do atomic do n := n + 1 end end` in the object left `n` unchanged at one thread too, and a function expression read a stale value and lost its writes. The cell is captured now, as a top-level `var`'s is, because a var field's `VarCodeGen` is a `MutableStaticBinding` (`VarCodeGen.java:207`; the three sites that ask are `CodeGen.java` `createTaskLexEnvVariables`, `taskConstructorDesc` and `constructWithFreeVars`). The defect had no ledger row. Evidence: `compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled` (old code: 'a function's reads 11 and 11 (expected 11 and 10), after a function's write 10 (expected 15), after a loop's writes 5 (expected 1007)'; the change: PASS). For the work: an immutable field is still captured by value, which is right.
4. **Every read and write of a `var` field now pays the transaction check and one indirection,** outside `atomic` too, as a mutable local and a top-level `var` do (row 641). Not timed. The two microGPT programs and the compiler's prelude declare no object with a var field (`grep` for `var` in an object's header or body over `explorations/run-c4/src/*.fss`, `explorations/apl/mg/*.fss` and the four prelude components finds only local variables).
5. **A `value` object with a `var` field compiles, and its `SEQV` changed.** `value object V(var n: ZZ32)`: `V(1) === V(1)` was `true` and is `false`, because `SEQV` compares a value object's JVM fields and a cell equals only itself (`nativeHelpers/equalityRule.java:83`). The specification forbids the declaration (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:35`); nothing refuses it on either path (row 112).
6. **`ant testQuick` on `67b1030c48`:** compiler 1625, othercompiler 263, library 86, no failure, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 7 minutes 2 seconds. The atomic loop of gate.md with `AtomicExprCompiled`, `AtomicFieldCompiled` and `VarFieldCapturedCompiled` added: 75 of 75 runs PASS at four threads. The distance stage's shadow patch applies: exit 0.

## For FACTS

**A compiled object's `var` field lives in a cell that the object holds, and an atomic expression is its body in an atomic block.** On the compiled path a `var` value parameter or `var` field of an object is a `MutableFValue` cell in a `public final` JVM field, made by the constructor; each read and write checks `BaseTask.inATransaction()` and goes through the transaction or the cell, by the code of a top-level `var` (`VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar`, a `MutableStaticBinding`), and a loop body or a function expression in the object's method captures the cell. A field without `var` holds its value and has no check. `atomic e` is compiled by `forAtomicBlock` on the block that holds `e`. What it means: a change of the transaction's variable code reaches fields with no second edit, and a new kind of nested context must capture a var field's cell as it does a top-level `var`'s. Tests: `compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled`, `compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled`, `compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-atomic-expr-field/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "The bytecode".

## The ledger

- **Close row 875:** `ledger.py close 875 --commit <the landing's commit> --test compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled.test`.
- **Close row 319:** `ledger.py close 319 --commit <the landing's commit> --test compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled.test`.
- **Rewrite row 641** (its notes said that a mutable field has no check; linted with `ledger.py check --rows`, 0 fail). The whole new line:

| 641 | compiled code calls `BaseTask.inATransaction()` before every read and write of a mutable local, top-level variable or `var` field, outside `atomic` too: about 1 to 2 ns a check, 64 % of a loop over an array with mutable locals (7 checks an element), 9 to 15 % of a scalar accumulator loop | NEGATIVE-BOUNDED | implementation gap (codegen) | silent | `explorations/perf-probes/transactions/run.sh` | transaction-check probe | Emitted by `compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java`: `LocalMutableVar` (a local), `MutableTaskVarCodeGen` (a variable captured by a task) and `MutableStaticBinding` (a top-level `var`; through `MutableFieldVar` an object's `var` field, whose cell the object holds), not by `MutableFValue`; an immutable field has no check. Measured on `8f0bc7389` at one thread by a shadow of `inATransaction()` returning `false`: TxArray 23.17 against 8.39 ns an element, TxScalar 20.42 against 18.67 ns. Not measured: four threads, code inside `atomic`, microGPT, a `var` field. Compiled path only: under walk `TxArray.fss` stops at load, `ZZ32Vector is undefined.` `explorations/perf-probes/transactions/REPORT.md`. |

- **Note on row 112** (fits: `ledger.py note 112 TEXT --check` leaves 3 characters of the notes and 243 of the row). The text to add:

  The compiled path compiles it too: `value object V(var n: ZZ32)` runs; with a `var` field kept in a cell, `V(1) === V(1)` is `false` (`true` before): `SEQV` compares cells by identity (`nativeHelpers/equalityRule.java:83`).

- **New rows:** none. The captured copy of finding 3 is repaired by the change that measured it and is asserted by its plain test.
- Rows read and left as they are: 397 (a tuple-typed var field's setter still fails verification; `compiler_tests/XXXTupleVarFieldCompiledRungC` still an expected failure), 322, 353, 948.

## Handover

Rung A landed on its branch at `67b1030c48`: the compiled path compiles `atomic e` and keeps an object's `var` field in a cell that a transaction tracks and that a loop body or a function expression captures; rows 875 and 319 close, row 641 takes a new line, row 112 a note; the gate's atomic runs gain `AtomicExprCompiled` and `AtomicFieldCompiled`, and `VarFieldCapturedCompiled` can join them; `tryatomic` (row 353), an atomic block or expression as a later argument (row 322) and plain writes beside a block (row 948) stand as they were.

## Revival change

### The change

- **An atomic expression compiles.** The team's code generator compiled `atomic do ... end` and had no case for `atomic e` over any other body: its `defaultCase` refused the node, 'Can't compile AtomicExpr' (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1776` and `forAtomicBlock` at `:1835`, at `c1ce2a35e1`). The tree now compiles `atomic e` as the atomic block that holds `e`, with the value of `e` (`compiler_tests/AtomicExprCompiled`). The reason: the specification gives the atomic expression its body's value and makes all its reads and writes one step (`Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex`, section "Atomic Expressions"), walk runs it, and the one library writes it (`Library/OneShotFlag.fss:18`).
- **A compiled object's `var` field is tracked by a transaction, at the cost of a check on every access.** The team's code generator read an object's field with a bare `GETFIELD` and wrote it with a bare `PUTFIELD`, a `var` field as any other (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:174-236` at `c1ce2a35e1`), so an `atomic` block did not track it: 40,000 `atomic do n := n + 1 end` on a field from a parallel loop gave 34,631 to 39,313 at four threads. The tree now keeps a `var` value parameter or `var` field in a cell that the object holds, read and written as a top-level `var` is; each access, outside `atomic` too, first asks whether a transaction is running (`compiler_tests/AtomicFieldCompiled`). A field without `var` is as it was. The reason: mutable fields of reference objects are mutable locations (`Specification/basic/evaluation/memory-ops.tex`, section "Memory and Memory Operations"), an atomic expression's reads and writes are all one step, and walk is exact on the same program.
- **A loop body or a function expression in an object's method works on the object's `var` field, not on a copy.** The team's code generator gave each task and closure a copy of a field's value, made when the task or closure was built, so a write from a loop body in the object's own method was lost, at one thread too, and a function expression read a stale value: `for i <- 1#k do atomic do n := n + 1 end end` in a method left `n` at 0. The tree now gives the task or closure the field's cell (`compiler_tests/VarFieldCapturedCompiled`). The reason: the measured failure, and walk's result on the same program.
- **Do not give a `value` object a `var` field in a compiled program.** The specification forbids it (`Specification/basic/objects.tex`, section "Value Objects") and nothing refuses it; with the field in a cell, two such objects built alike are no longer strictly equivalent, `V(1) === V(1)` is `false`.

### Provenance

- The atomic expression: ledger row 875; the batch record `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-31.md`, rung A; climb batch 31.
- The field in a cell: ledger row 319; fork A1 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-31.md`, "Forks the batch takes", whose default it builds ("A `var` field is kept in a cell, as a top-level `var` is"); P-169, whose store and slots are untouched; climb batch 31, rung A.
- The captured cell: measured by rung A of climb batch 31 while building fork A1; no row; a consequence of A1's default.
- The value object: ledger row 112, with the note above.
